Fill in the blanks so that the following reasoning is correct:

The notation $5 \not\mid 16$ means ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/fb6fbc91b2218218acab5a0fe1baed797fc7ece0800c3280bc0d53af6d765ae3.svg) It is equivalent to the statement that for $\[6pt]$ ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/48442365817dc8d3a14cc2f5931284b07e8cbfccf0bd2a097f7362f0f97348cb.svg)
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/20865eee0320e3c8d4822421723a5a251048e7158888ac6416427f632bcb85b7.svg) we have ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/45453872ffd37b70f166312cf1aa4c3966437e91dc293ac0db198d895e41821c.svg)
question.worked_solution:
The notation $a \not\mid b$ means $a$ does not divide $b.$ So, $5 \not\mid 16$ means ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114596/assets/833ccbc866a4951df8fa798f0780922c3dc56bff0b2baf1a36711c3f47c9f313.svg)

According to the definition of integer divisibility, the fact that $a$ does not divide $b$ means that for any integer $k,$ we have that 

$$
b \neq a k.
$$

 

Therefore, $5 \not\mid 16$ is equivalent to the statement that for $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm{ any}}$ $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm{integer}}$ $k,$ we have $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}16 \neq 5k}.$
